sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我和 Katie 博士将带你了解成人自闭症诊断的迹象、流程以及这段旅程的真实样貌。

sentences.zh: 我是 Marianne 博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: With no further ado, let's dive in and catch up on my chat with Dr. Katie Adolphus, where we're looking at adult autism assessment and diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们直接进入主题，回顾我与 Katie Adolphus 博士的谈话，我们将探讨成人自闭症的评估与诊断。

sentences.en: I will catch you on the other side.
sentences.zh: 稍后见。

sentences.en: Hi, Katie, Dr. Katie Adolphus.
sentences.zh: 嗨，Katie，Katie Adolphus 博士。

sentences.en: Welcome to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到播客。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢你能来。

sentences.en: You are a clinical psychologist and you specialise in working with people of all ages who might fit within a diagnostic criteria for autism and or for ADHD.
sentences.zh: 你是一位临床心理学家，专门从事各年龄段人群的工作，这些人可能符合自闭症和/或多动症的诊断标准。

sentences.en: Today, we are thinking about autism.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来谈谈自闭症。

sentences.en: Thank you for pitching this episode to me.
sentences.zh: 感谢你向我提议这一期节目。

sentences.en: Could you tell us a little bit, in case someone has no idea, what is autism and how might people observe that?
sentences.zh: 你能为那些完全不了解的人简单介绍一下，什么是自闭症，人们可能会如何观察到它吗？

sentences.en: In themselves or others?
sentences.zh: 在他们自己或他人身上？

sentences.en: I'm very happy to.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意。

sentences.en: So autism is considered to be a neurological difference.
sentences.zh: 自闭症被认为是一种神经学上的差异。

sentences.en: So it's about how your brain has developed and it impacts or influences how people see the world from a sensory point of view, from a social and relationship point of view,
sentences.zh: 所以它关乎你的大脑是如何发育的，它影响或左右着人们从感官角度、社交和人际关系角度看待世界的方式，

sentences.en: and in terms of kind of their communication style and preferences.
sentences.zh: 以及他们的沟通风格和偏好。

sentences.en: So it's a difference rather than a deficit or a disorder.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种差异，而不是缺陷或障碍。

sentences.en: And so it has equal value.
sentences.zh: 因此它具有同等的价值。

sentences.en: But those are some of the domains in which you might notice differences.
sentences.zh: 但这些是你可能会注意到差异的一些领域。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And adult autism diagnosis are very much becoming more spoken about more recently.
sentences.zh: 而且成人自闭症诊断最近确实被谈论得更多了。

sentences.en: Can I ask what triggers or what things might happen in someone's adult life that might make them begin to question whether they might be autistic, Katie?
sentences.zh: 我可以问一下，Katie，一个人的成年生活中可能会发生什么触发因素或事情，让他们开始质疑自己是否可能是自闭症患者吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So one of the really common ones is that a child of theirs has been identified as autistic or neurodivergent,
sentences.zh: 其中一个非常常见的情况是，他们的孩子被认定为自闭症患者或神经多样性人士，

sentences.en: which is the kind of umbrella term for lots of different neurodevelopmental differences and that that has made them kind of look back and reflect on their own childhood,
sentences.zh: 这是涵盖许多不同神经发育差异的总称，这让他们开始回顾和反思自己的童年，

sentences.en: their own experiences and how they are understanding the world that brings them to a point of wanting clarification for themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己的经历以及他们理解世界的方式，这使他们想要为自己寻求明确的答案。

sentences.en: But it might also be somebody who's had some struggles in the workplace and struggles to reach their potential or those kind of relationship hiccups that are having an impact on their well-being.
sentences.zh: 但也可能是某人在职场中遇到了一些困难，难以发挥潜力，或者那些对他们的幸福感产生影响的人际关系挫折。

sentences.en: Lots of adults talk about having their intentions misunderstood so that they come at a situation giving making really clear and direct communication and that's interpreted as rude or brusque or and which is absolutely not that person's intent.
sentences.zh: 许多成年人谈到他们的意图被误解，他们明明在沟通时表达得非常清晰直接，却被解读为粗鲁或生硬，而这绝对不是当事人的本意。

sentences.en: And similarly, obviously, it can work the other way where they're struggling to read somebody else's intent in the way that that other person.
sentences.zh: 同样地，显然，反过来也一样，他们可能难以解读对方的意图，

sentences.en: Is intending.
sentences.zh: 即对方真正想要表达的意思。

sentences.en: So those kind of challenges within kind of the relationships that they experience in the world can often bring bring someone to wonder about whether they're autistic.
sentences.zh: 所以，在他们所经历的人际关系中出现的这类挑战，往往会让人开始怀疑自己是否是自闭症患者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And just as you were talking, it was making me think about my current context, which I'll explain before we start to speak.
sentences.zh: 就在你说话的时候，让我想到了我目前的情况，在开始谈话前我会解释一下。

sentences.en: I've hurt my neck and so I'm just fresh back from physio.
sentences.zh: 我伤了脖子，所以刚从理疗回来。

sentences.en: And I'm kind of imagining whether someone is kind of realizing there's resistance in the way they are socially, the way they're engaging with the world.
sentences.zh: 我在想，是否有人意识到他们在社交方式、与世界互动的方式上存在阻碍。

sentences.en: And actually, sometimes even the process of assessment and diagnosis can free that up so that they understand themselves better or so that they can engage more fully and, I guess,
sentences.zh: 事实上，有时甚至评估和诊断的过程本身就能释放这种阻碍，让他们更好地了解自己，或者让他们能够更充分地参与，我想，

sentences.en: optimally thrive.
sentences.zh: 以最佳状态茁壮成长。

sentences.en: Does that does that sound about right, Katie?
sentences.zh: Katie，听起来是这样吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And this is about one of my my passion for the area is because I'm interested in people's stories and the stories that we tell ourselves about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我之所以对这个领域充满热情，是因为我对人们的故事以及我们对自己讲述的故事很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And if you're autistic, but haven't known that framework to understand yourself,
sentences.zh: 如果你是自闭症患者，但之前不知道这个框架来理解自己，

sentences.en: you will have told yourself many stories about how you're doing and other people will have contributed to that as well.
sentences.zh: 你一定对自己讲述过许多关于你表现如何的故事，而其他人也会对此有所贡献。

sentences.en: And so to having a story that actually what you're describing,
sentences.zh: 所以，拥有一个故事，实际上就是你所描述的，

sentences.en: there's a community of people who experience the world in similar ways and there is a way of understanding it so that it is not that you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 有一群人以类似的方式体验世界，并且有一种理解它的方式，这样你就不是错的。

sentences.en: It's not that you're broken.
sentences.zh: 你不是坏掉的。

sentences.en: It's not that you're mad or crazy or whatever else you might have wondered about for yourself.
sentences.zh: 你不是疯了或疯狂，或者任何你可能对自己产生过的怀疑。

sentences.en: But it is that there is a difference and therefore you can advocate for what you need to thrive and develop and build a life around those things that bring you joy,
sentences.zh: 而是存在一种差异，因此你可以为自己需要的东西辩护，以茁壮成长、发展，并围绕那些带给你快乐的事情建立生活，

sentences.en: bring you replenishment and build strategies around those bits of life that challenge.
sentences.zh: 带给你充实感，并围绕生活中那些具有挑战性的部分建立策略。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And are there different ways that people of different genders may kind of exhibit signs of perhaps being autistic or things that they're struggling with or maybe even finding easier kind of what are the what are the gender profiles,
sentences.zh: 那么，不同性别的人在表现出可能是自闭症的迹象，或者他们正在挣扎的事情，甚至可能觉得更容易的事情方面，是否有不同的方式？性别特征是什么，

sentences.en: Katie?
sentences.zh: Katie？

sentences.en: That's a really interesting question, because historically, what we understood to be autism is what we now understand to be a typically male way of experiencing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题，因为从历史上看，我们所理解的自闭症是我们现在所理解的典型的男性体验方式。

sentences.en: Autism or an external way, a way that's observable to others.
sentences.zh: 自闭症或外在的方式，一种对他人可见的方式。

sentences.en: And so the the it used to be that many more boys and men were thought to be autistic than girls and women.
sentences.zh: 所以过去人们认为自闭症男孩和男性比女孩和女性多得多。

sentences.en: Nowadays, there's a real sense of an understanding of there's an internal experience of being autistic as well, but it's less observable to the observer.
sentences.zh: 如今，人们真正意识到自闭症也存在内在体验，只是对观察者来说不太明显。

sentences.en: But it's very much experienced and can be very, very impactful and very important to understand.
sentences.zh: 但它确实被深刻体验，并且可能非常有影响力，理解这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: So this started being described as the kind of girls version, girls and women's and female version of autism.
sentences.zh: 所以这开始被描述为所谓的“女孩版”，女孩和女性的女性版自闭症。

sentences.en: And now it's better, I think, described as the internal experience of autism, which means that oftentimes girls, women,
sentences.zh: 现在我认为最好将其描述为自闭症的内在体验，这意味着通常女孩、女性、

sentences.en: non-binary and some male people experience the internal version of autism.
sentences.zh: 非二元性别者和一些男性会体验到内在版本的自闭症。

sentences.en: And so when you're when we're helping people discover that, you know, we're really being mindful about what's your internal experience of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们帮助人们发现这一点时，你知道，我们真的在关注你对世界的内在体验是什么。

sentences.en: You know, you might be doing X, Y and Z that neurotypical people might be doing as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可能正在做 X、Y 和 Z，神经典型的人可能也在做。

sentences.en: But what's your experience of doing that?
sentences.zh: 但你做这些事情的体验是什么？

sentences.en: What's the cost of doing that to you, your well-being and your energy levels?
sentences.zh: 做这些事情对你、你的幸福感和你的能量水平有什么代价？

sentences.en: Yeah, what it costs you to engage in your normal life or to be able to go out there and earn money and kind of do all the things.
sentences.zh: 是的，为了过正常生活或能够出去赚钱并完成所有事情，你付出了什么代价？

sentences.en: Is that is that masking or is that something beyond masking?
sentences.zh: 那是掩饰（masking）吗，还是超越了掩饰的东西？

sentences.en: I think it can be described as masking and masking is when you work and it can be conscious or unconscious.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可以被描述为掩饰，掩饰是指你所做的工作，它可以是有意识的，也可以是无意识的。

sentences.en: But when you are kind of going against your internal, authentic way of being to be safe in the world, to present as somebody without differences and who fits,
sentences.zh: 但当你为了在世界上保持安全，为了表现得像一个没有差异、能够融入的人，而违背你内在、真实的自我时，

sentences.en: who fits the majority way of being, the majority population.
sentences.zh: 融入大多数人的生活方式，大多数人口。

sentences.en: And as I said, it can be conscious because I'm not presenting all of myself to you in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这可以是有意识的，因为我并没有在这个播客中展示我的全部。

sentences.en: There's parts of me that I'm squishing down and masking and that's a conscious choice and OK.
sentences.zh: 我有部分自我正在压抑和掩饰，这是一个有意识的选择，没关系。

sentences.en: But it can also be unconscious where you've just learned through through life's experiences that that bit of you makes you vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 但它也可能是无意识的，你只是通过生活经验了解到，你的那一部分让你变得脆弱。

sentences.en: So you so it's not it's not safe to to be that way.
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得那样做是不安全的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like socially conditioned.
sentences.zh: 就像社会条件反射一样。

sentences.en: That's undesirable.
sentences.zh: 那是不受欢迎的。

sentences.en: That's not OK.
sentences.zh: 那是不可以的。

sentences.en: Don't do that.
sentences.zh: 别那样做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Don't don't flap in this way, but it might be OK if you flick your hair.
sentences.zh: 别那样拍打，但如果你拨弄头发可能没关系。

sentences.en: So some of the ways to cope with life might involve what people call stimming.
sentences.zh: 所以一些应对生活的方式可能涉及人们所说的“自我刺激”（stimming）。

sentences.en: Which might include flapping any or any other kind of stimming activities that people might see in others or in themselves.
sentences.zh: 这可能包括拍打或人们在他人或自己身上可能看到的任何其他类型的自我刺激活动。

sentences.en: So sometimes that it might be physical movements, click, you know, or clicking or saying different words or I mean, if you think about it, actually laughing is a stim.
sentences.zh: 所以有时可能是身体动作，点击，你知道，或者发出点击声或说不同的词，或者我的意思是，如果你仔细想想，实际上大笑也是一种自我刺激。

sentences.en: Stim because a stim is a repetitive movement that happens to kind of help regulate emotion.
sentences.zh: 自我刺激，因为自我刺激是一种重复性的动作，有助于调节情绪。

sentences.en: And so laughing is a funny thing we do with our breathing and our voice box when we're feeling a big emotion, whether that's hilarity or embarrassment or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们感受到强烈的情绪时，无论是欢闹、尴尬还是其他什么，大笑是我们用呼吸和声带做的一件有趣的事情。

sentences.en: As long when the emotion gets that big, we do a thing.
sentences.zh: 只要情绪达到那种程度，我们就会做一件事。

sentences.en: So and that's what stims are in lots of ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，在很多方面，这就是自我刺激。

sentences.en: So there's lots of different types kind of fiddling with hair, fiddling with your clothes, pacing up and down when you're stressed.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多不同的类型，比如摆弄头发、摆弄衣服、压力大时来回踱步。

sentences.en: There's all sorts of things that that and they stand out from typical more or less in different ways.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的东西，它们以不同的方式或多或少地从典型行为中脱颖而出。

sentences.en: Yeah, so obviously everybody, you know, either with an autism presentation or not, will self-stimulate at times.
sentences.zh: 是的，显然每个人，无论是否有自闭症表现，有时都会进行自我刺激。

sentences.en: But actually there's certain key stims and if used repetitively and perhaps not always in conjunction with, I don't know, is this the wrong term?
sentences.zh: 但实际上有一些关键的自我刺激，如果重复使用，也许并不总是与，我不知道，这是错误的术语吗？

sentences.en: But more kind of socially accepted ways of stimulating ourselves, like or regulating ourselves, like a soothing rhythm breath, for example.
sentences.zh: 但更多的是社会所接受的自我刺激方式，或者调节自己的方式，比如舒缓的节奏呼吸，例如。

sentences.en: That's what we tend to advocate to people.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们倾向于向人们提倡的。

sentences.en: But actually if spinning around or flapping, you know, is doing the same thing, but you certainly get a few more stern looks if you're if you're doing that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果旋转或拍打，你知道，起到了同样的作用，但如果你那样做，肯定会得到更多严厉的目光。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, because I don't think people probably think of laughing and those other things that we've described as stims in that way.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我不认为人们会把大笑和我们描述的其他事情看作是那种方式的自我刺激。

sentences.en: But I think autistic people can use stims to help regulate perhaps more.
sentences.zh: 但我认为自闭症患者可能更多地使用自我刺激来帮助调节。

sentences.en: I don't know that there's research to check that,
sentences.zh: 我不知道是否有研究来证实这一点，

sentences.en: but that's my experience than neurotypical people and maybe in place of putting words to their internal kind of emotional experience.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是我的经验，比神经典型的人更多，也许是代替了用语言来表达他们内在的情绪体验。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd never thought about laughing as being a stim.
sentences.zh: 是的，我从来没想过大笑是一种自我刺激。

sentences.en: I know, right.
sentences.zh: 我知道，对吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: OK, so people that laugh a lot, that might be more of a stimulatory behaviour.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以经常大笑的人，那可能更多是一种刺激性行为。

sentences.en: I think I was I was mentioning that in the context of saying actually stimming is an experience that we all share, whether we're neurotypical or neurodivergent.
sentences.zh: 我想我提到这一点是在说，实际上自我刺激是我们所有人共享的体验，无论我们是神经典型还是神经多样性。

sentences.en: So that's one way in which there's a shared experience.
sentences.zh: 所以这是共享体验的一种方式。

sentences.en: But that isn't to say I think autistic people use stims more.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说我认为自闭症患者使用自我刺激更多。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So there's no there's no correlation between laughing and autism.
sentences.zh: 所以大笑和自闭症之间没有关联。

sentences.en: This is an example of self-stilling.
sentences.zh: 这只是自我调节的一个例子。

sentences.en: It's just a way in which experience is similar.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种体验相似的方式。

sentences.en: I'm with you.
sentences.zh: 我懂你的意思。

sentences.en: I'm with you.
sentences.zh: 我懂你的意思。

sentences.en: Thank you for clarifying that.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的澄清。

sentences.en: So, you know, I guess if people have got to this stage of the podcast episode, they'll be thinking, yeah, I think ticks a box, ticks a box, ticks a box.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我想如果人们已经听到了播客的这一阶段，他们会想，是的，我觉得这符合，这符合，这符合。

sentences.en: What are the processes involved with getting an autism assessment for an adult?
sentences.zh: 成年人进行自闭症评估的过程涉及什么？

sentences.en: So different NHS trusts do it in different ways.
sentences.zh: 不同的 NHS 信托机构以不同的方式进行。

sentences.en: But your GP will be your first port of call to go through the NHS.
sentences.zh: 但你的全科医生（GP）将是你通过 NHS 进行评估的第一联系人。

sentences.en: There's also the system of going through right to choose providers.
sentences.zh: 还有通过“选择权”（Right to Choose）提供商的系统。

sentences.en: So I can talk to my own experience of offering adult assessments in the independent sector.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以谈谈我在独立部门提供成人评估的经验。

sentences.en: That's a system whereby contracts have been set up with different providers to provide a service for NHS clients that remains free at the point of need.
sentences.zh: 这是一个系统，通过该系统与不同的提供商签订合同，为 NHS 客户提供服务，在需要时保持免费。

sentences.en: So you can go to your GP and ask for consideration of being put on the right to choose pathway for an assessment.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以去找你的全科医生，要求考虑将你纳入“选择权”途径进行评估。

sentences.en: And there are criteria for whether you can join those pathways and those waiting lists.
sentences.zh: 而且对于你是否可以加入这些途径和等待名单有相应的标准。

sentences.en: I don't have details about that because that's not my I don't my service doesn't do right to choose assessments.
sentences.zh: 我没有关于那方面的详细信息，因为那不是我的，我的服务不进行“选择权”评估。

sentences.en: But that's a possibility for people within the independent sector.
sentences.zh: 但这对独立部门的人来说是一种可能性。

sentences.en: So for us, people make an inquiry and can book an appointment to get an initial it's like a screening appointment that talks through what brings them to wonder about an assessment.
sentences.zh: 所以对我们来说，人们进行咨询并可以预约进行初步评估，这就像是一个筛查预约，讨论是什么让他们想要进行评估。

sentences.en: And it's really to make sure that an assessment makes sense and isn't a use of resources that isn't meaningful.
sentences.zh: 这真的是为了确保评估是有意义的，而不是对资源的无意义使用。

sentences.en: And then the assessment itself is like a deep dive into someone's experiences in childhood right through up to adulthood, their experience of learning, friendships,
sentences.zh: 然后评估本身就像是对一个人从童年到成年经历的深入挖掘，他们对学习、友谊、

sentences.en: relationships of the sensory world or what's it like, you know, flexibility and plan versus the need for predictability.
sentences.zh: 人际关系、感官世界的体验，或者是什么样的，你知道，灵活性和计划与对可预测性的需求。

sentences.en: And we do we we we cover that ground in a number of different appointments and doing a number of different tasks just to explore how someone approaches the world.
sentences.zh: 我们会在多次不同的预约中涵盖这些内容，并进行多项不同的任务，只是为了探索一个人是如何接触世界的。

sentences.en: And we ask whether they've got people in their family or network who would they would be comfortable to contribute.
sentences.zh: 我们会询问他们是否有家人或社交圈里的人，愿意配合提供相关信息。

sentences.en: So we might ask a parent to give us some information about what they remember of their child in their childhood or a partner, perhaps, that could contribute something.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会请家长提供一些关于他们孩子童年时期的记忆，或者请伴侣提供一些有价值的信息。

sentences.en: And then we pull all of that information together to reach a decision about the possibility of them being autistic.
sentences.zh: 然后我们将所有这些信息汇总起来，以判断他们是否可能患有自闭症。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: So there's not kind of the practical elements as such, like you might see in children with with an ADOS assessment, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不像你们在儿童 ADOS 评估中看到的那种实际操作环节。

sentences.en: It's much more kind of conversational and relational.
sentences.zh: 它更多是基于对话和人际关系的。

sentences.en: It is it is more conversational in with adults and some services, including ours.
sentences.zh: 对于成年人来说，包括我们的一些服务在内，确实更多是对话式的。

sentences.en: We do still do the ADOS, but the adults, the ADOS that we do for adults is still fairly conversational.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然会进行 ADOS 评估，但针对成年人的 ADOS 评估依然相当侧重于对话。

sentences.en: There's a few tasks, but it's not as task heavy as the the children's, as the ADOS that we might do for children.
sentences.zh: 虽然有一些任务，但并不像儿童 ADOS 评估那样任务繁重。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I was in a school meeting recently and there was a copy of that book.
sentences.zh: 我最近在学校开会时看到过那本书。

sentences.en: Is it called Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 是叫《星期二》吗？

sentences.en: It's got frogs in it.
sentences.zh: 里面有青蛙。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that was in the ADOS at one stage.
sentences.zh: 对，我想那曾经是 ADOS 评估的一部分。

sentences.en: And there's no words.
sentences.zh: 而且书里没有文字。

sentences.en: There's always there's no words in it.
sentences.zh: 它一直都是没有文字的。

sentences.en: And I said to the teacher, I said, did you know, actually,
sentences.zh: 我当时跟老师说，你知道吗，其实，

sentences.en: this is commonly used as kind of a screen for trying to trying to work out what might be going on and what people's understanding of that is.
sentences.zh: 这本书常被用作一种筛查工具，用来了解人们对事物的理解方式。

sentences.en: And it's used as part of autism assessment.
sentences.zh: 它被用作自闭症评估的一部分。

sentences.en: You're just like, no, I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 你当时肯定想，不，我完全不知道。

sentences.en: We just use it as a picture book.
sentences.zh: 我们只是把它当作绘本用。

sentences.en: Well, actually, you know, you can use it in that way to kind of think about free screening.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实你可以用这种方式来思考初步筛查。

sentences.en: Is there anything that someone could do if they're preparing for going in for an initial assessment to prepare for that kind of optimally?
sentences.zh: 如果有人准备去进行初步评估，他们可以做些什么来达到最佳的准备状态吗？

sentences.en: So maybe we used to do developmental assessment reports in in clinic.
sentences.zh: 以前我们诊所可能会做发育评估报告。

sentences.en: Could they have those conversations with their with their parents, with with people who knew them when they were a child and think about all of that?
sentences.zh: 他们是否可以和父母，或者那些从小就认识他们的人进行交流，去回顾所有这些经历？

sentences.en: What are top questions or top ways of preparing, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为最好的准备方式或核心问题是什么？

sentences.en: I think what we often mention to adults is to just spend some time ahead of the appointments, reminiscing and kind of maybe that's talking with parents, as you say,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们经常建议成年人花点时间在预约前进行回忆，正如你所说，可以和父母谈谈，

sentences.en: or siblings about and thinking about, OK, where was I when I started primary?
sentences.zh: 或者和兄弟姐妹聊聊，思考一下：我上小学时在哪里？

sentences.en: Where did I live?
sentences.zh: 我住在哪里？

sentences.en: What school did I go to?
sentences.zh: 我上了哪所学校？

sentences.en: So just trying to really put yourself in those times, because then accessing memories of those times will be easier.
sentences.zh: 试着真正让自己回到那个时代，因为这样更容易唤起当时的记忆。

sentences.en: So it might be looking through school reports or photos from school days, anything,
sentences.zh: 所以可以翻翻学校报告或学生时代的旧照片，任何东西，

sentences.en: anything that can just bring those early years to the kind of more accessible bit of your of your memory, really.
sentences.zh: 任何能让你更容易触及早年记忆的东西，真的很有用。

sentences.en: So that can be really helpful so that, you know, that they've done some digging around in their life experience before they get to us.
sentences.zh: 这非常有帮助，因为在见到我们之前，他们已经对自己的人生经历做了一些挖掘。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And if someone is kind of heavily defended or so used to masking, can it be hard to kind of really work out whether they do fulfill that diagnostic criteria?
sentences.zh: 如果一个人防御心理很强，或者习惯了掩饰，那么要确定他们是否符合诊断标准会很难吗？

sentences.en: Can you always kind of sieve out what needs to what needs to come through?
sentences.zh: 你能总是筛选出需要呈现的信息吗？

sentences.en: I think that's something that actually a lot of people are worried about,
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是很多人担心的问题，

sentences.en: that the fact that they've gone a lifetime so far without it being identified might either mean that it doesn't exist and they're making it all up and they're over exaggerating concerns or what have you,
sentences.zh: 他们担心自己活了这么久都没被发现，是不是意味着自己根本没有自闭症，只是在编造或夸大问题，诸如此类，

sentences.en: or that an assessment process won't uncover it.
sentences.zh: 或者担心评估过程无法发现它。

sentences.en: So we work really hard to get underneath the mask and actually sometimes that's why the ADOS can be helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常努力地去揭开伪装，其实有时候这就是 ADOS 评估有用的原因。

sentences.en: It's not without its issues, but it can be helpful because it's kind of odd.
sentences.zh: 它并非没有问题，但它确实有帮助，因为它有点奇怪。

sentences.en: Some of the tasks and things that we do are just slightly odd.
sentences.zh: 我们做的一些任务和事情就是有点古怪。

sentences.en: So it's unlikely that you've kind of created a script for it or, you know, kind of quite prepared for it.
sentences.zh: 所以你不太可能提前写好剧本，或者为此做好充分准备。

sentences.en: So in that in that kind of way, it can be a helpful way to get underneath the mask.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，它确实是揭开伪装的一种有效方式。

sentences.en: And there are other kind of adult based assessment tools that help us do that as well to get underneath the mask.
sentences.zh: 还有其他针对成年人的评估工具也能帮助我们做到这一点，揭开伪装。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's making me think of when I was training in my doctorate in clinical psychology and they were like, actually,
sentences.zh: 是的，这让我想起我在攻读临床心理学博士时，他们说，其实，

sentences.en: when you are a clinical psychologist and you're familiar with all these measures,
sentences.zh: 当你成为临床心理学家并熟悉所有这些测量方法时，

sentences.en: it does actually make it a bit harder to test you latterly because you know the answers and you know what's coming.
sentences.zh: 反而更难对你进行测试，因为你知道答案，也知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Are there certain professions that are more likely to have an autism diagnosis, to be autistic or kind of to be gravitating towards that?
sentences.zh: 有些职业是否更容易出现自闭症诊断，或者更容易吸引自闭症人士？

sentences.en: I know that always when I was working in CAMHS, for example, we found so I was working in West Midlands, very close to kind of Jaguar engineering bases.
sentences.zh: 我记得以前在 CAMHS 工作时，比如，我当时在西米德兰兹工作，离捷豹工程基地很近。

sentences.en: And it was said that actually, this is a kind of almost a hotbed of of children and young people with autism presentations,
sentences.zh: 当时有人说，这几乎是自闭症儿童和青少年的温床，

sentences.en: whether they're diagnosed or not, because their mums or their dads or both are actually engineers.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是否被诊断出来，因为他们的父母双方或其中一方其实是工程师。

sentences.en: And that was thought to be kind of something that naturally lots of people with autism would gravitate towards.
sentences.zh: 人们认为这是一种自闭症人士会自然倾向的领域。

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 这有道理吗？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I don't know what the current sense is about that specifically, but I remember historically there being research around, you know, certain,
sentences.zh: 我不知道目前对此的具体看法如何，但我记得历史上曾有关于某些职业的研究，

sentences.en: but if we think about it more broadly from certain professions, but think about kind of what is the cognitive style of someone who's autistic.
sentences.zh: 如果我们从更广泛的职业角度去思考，不妨想想自闭症人士的认知风格是什么。

sentences.en: And so autistic people are ordinarily fantastic at paying attention to one thing at a time.
sentences.zh: 自闭症人士通常非常擅长一次专注于一件事。

sentences.en: And they can often do that above and beyond the kind of attention span of a neurotypical person.
sentences.zh: 他们往往能做到超越神经典型人士的专注力。

sentences.en: So and have those really highly specialized, highly specific areas of interest and depth of knowledge and understanding.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有高度专业、高度具体的兴趣领域，以及深厚的知识和理解力。

sentences.en: So professions or disciplines that require that suit an autistic way of being in the world.
sentences.zh: 因此，需要这种特质的职业或学科，非常适合自闭症人士的生存方式。

sentences.en: Autistic minds are really good at that kind of all or nothing.
sentences.zh: 自闭症思维非常擅长那种非黑即白的逻辑。

sentences.en: Something is either true or false, right or wrong in really clear ways.
sentences.zh: 事情要么是真的要么是假的，要么对要么错，界限非常清晰。

sentences.en: So professions that might be served by having that perspective and where communication is really clear and explicit.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些受益于这种视角，且沟通非常清晰明确的职业就很适合。

sentences.en: So, you know, there'll be some areas of law where having that real clarity of thought about, well, this means that.
sentences.zh: 比如，在法律的某些领域，拥有这种清晰的思维方式，即“这代表那个”，

sentences.en: And the other thing means the other thing can bring a real strength to that field.
sentences.zh: 而“那个代表另一个”，能为该领域带来真正的优势。

sentences.en: So it's about fields that the benefit from an autistic way of being.
sentences.zh: 所以这关乎那些受益于自闭症生存方式的领域。

sentences.en: And there might be other disciplines or professions or ways of living your adult life that that lend themselves to people who who don't need as much social interaction to keep their social tank of energy full.
sentences.zh: 可能还有其他学科、职业或生活方式，适合那些不需要太多社交互动来维持社交能量储备的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, we are all so different, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们每个人都非常不同，不是吗？

sentences.en: That would be a terrible job for me.
sentences.zh: 那对我来说会是一份糟糕的工作。

sentences.en: I love speaking with people.
sentences.zh: 我热爱与人交谈。

sentences.en: I love random conversations with people.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢和人进行随意的对话。

sentences.en: You know, I'm the sort of person that will chat to someone in Tesco, you know, over the cauliflowers like, you know, but we're all so very different.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是那种会在乐购超市里，对着花椰菜跟人聊天的人，但我们每个人确实非常不同。

sentences.en: But actually, what we know is that people can can reach what's called autistic burnout when when they're really struggling, you know,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们知道人们在苦苦挣扎时，可能会达到所谓的“自闭症倦怠”，你知道，

sentences.en: with the with the resources they've got to be able to do all the things that that that life that life necessitates.
sentences.zh: 当他们拥有的资源不足以应付生活所必需的一切事情时。

sentences.en: Could you tell us a bit more about autistic burnout?
sentences.zh: 你能多讲讲自闭症倦怠吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So it's a term that the autistic community have kind of I don't know if the autistic community were the first to kind of use it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个自闭症群体使用的术语，我不知道是不是他们最先开始用的，

sentences.en: But certainly it really resonates with lots of people's experience.
sentences.zh: 但它确实引起了许多人的共鸣。

sentences.en: And it describes that chronic, ongoing emotional kind of and cognitive and social exhaustion that being neurodivergent in a neurotypical world can generate.
sentences.zh: 它描述了在神经典型世界中作为神经多样性人士所产生的长期的、持续的情感、认知和社会层面的耗竭。

sentences.en: And so if you're in that chronic state of using up more resources than you've got because the world requires that of you,
sentences.zh: 如果你处于那种长期消耗的资源超过你所拥有的状态，因为世界对你有这样的要求，

sentences.en: then you stay in that depletion and kind of you're in energy debt, so to speak, which can have an impact on how well or otherwise you manage and you function in the world.
sentences.zh: 那么你就会一直处于这种枯竭状态，也就是所谓的“能量负债”，这会影响你在世界上的应对和运作能力。

sentences.en: So burnout can look like losing areas of functioning that have previously been OK for you.
sentences.zh: 所以倦怠可能表现为丧失了以前还能正常运作的功能领域。

sentences.en: So you might eat less,
sentences.zh: 比如你可能会吃得更少，

sentences.en: be unable to speak for a period and just just need to be in bed by yourself for long stretches because the world the world is hard and exhausting without without it being set up for you.
sentences.zh: 可能会有一段时间无法说话，只能长时间独自待在床上，因为这个世界对你来说既艰难又令人疲惫，而且它并没有为你而设。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for helping us understand a bit more about that.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你帮我们进一步了解了这一点。

sentences.en: And when people kind of receive a diagnosis, you know, they might respond in a variety of different ways.
sentences.zh: 当人们收到诊断结果时，他们的反应可能多种多样。

sentences.en: It might feel like, oh, finally,
sentences.zh: 可能会感觉，哦，终于，

sentences.en: like I feel like I know myself and I can kind of get out there and tell people about me and people will understand me better or I will care less about what other people think of me.
sentences.zh: 感觉我终于了解自己了，我可以走出去告诉别人关于我的事，别人也会更好地理解我，或者我会更不在乎别人怎么看我。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like, is it is it always a good thing?
sentences.zh: 这总是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: Does it sometimes feel like a negative thing or like the shame or judgment or blame or it's kind of their fault?
sentences.zh: 有时会感觉是件坏事吗？比如感到羞耻、评判、指责，或者觉得是他们自己的错？

sentences.en: That's an internalized process there.
sentences.zh: 那是一个内在化的过程。

sentences.en: That's a really, really important question, because we shouldn't be doing it if it's not ultimately helpful and meaningful.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常非常重要的问题，因为如果它最终没有帮助和意义，我们就不应该这样做。

sentences.en: My experience in talking with people is that and what I witness often starts with relief, you know,
sentences.zh: 我在与人交谈中的经验是，我所见到的往往始于一种解脱，你知道，

sentences.en: to kind of to have reached the point where you have wondered why the world seems more difficult to navigate for you than it does for others.
sentences.zh: 终于到了一个点，你不再疑惑为什么这个世界对你来说比对别人更难驾驭。

sentences.en: I suddenly got a framework around it to understand that, which brings with it things that might be helpful to make life less difficult to navigate.
sentences.zh: 我突然有了一个框架来理解它，这带来了一些可能有用的东西，让生活变得不那么难以驾驭。

sentences.en: So it often starts with relief.
sentences.zh: 所以它通常始于解脱。

sentences.en: I think there are also in the journey periods of time where it's like, oh, blindly, but that's lifelong.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这个过程中也会有一段时间觉得，哦，天哪，这是终身的。

sentences.en: So that means it's going to always be difficult and that's hard.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它将永远很困难，这很难接受。

sentences.en: You know, so I think that's potentially a stage or a position that people kind of go in and out of as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以我认为这也是人们进进出出的一个阶段或状态。

sentences.en: And I think there can be elements of grief and loss about, gosh, if this was understood about me in earlier years, how different could things have been?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为也会有悲伤和失落的成分，比如，天哪，如果早年人们能理解我这一点，事情会有多不同？

sentences.en: And I think what the joy of doing this work is a relief in the beginning and then the kind of coming through the processing of this framework to your life,
sentences.zh: 我认为做这份工作的乐趣在于最初的解脱，然后是处理这个框架并将其应用到你的生活中，

sentences.en: coming to a point of validation and acceptance and strength and a way of building self-compassion, building self-esteem,
sentences.zh: 最终达到一种认可、接纳和力量的状态，并建立起自我同情和自尊，

sentences.en: which just are so vital to wellbeing and emotional and mental health, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 这些对幸福感以及情绪和心理健康至关重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, I think especially since the pandemic, the way the world is now very much, I think,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，特别是在疫情之后，现在的世界环境在很大程度上，我认为，

sentences.en: encourages us to make our own bespoke way of existing in the world in a way that does suit us, suit our own individual needs, our family needs, you know, just our preferences.
sentences.zh: 鼓励我们以适合自己的方式去生活，去满足我们个人的需求、家庭的需求，你知道，仅仅是我们的偏好。

sentences.en: And it's almost like we can paint by numbers now, we can really have our lives, I don't know, vibe with us, not just, you know, one size fits all.
sentences.zh: 这就像我们现在可以按需涂色，我们可以真正让生活与我们产生共鸣，而不是那种“一刀切”的模式。

sentences.en: So employment doesn't suit everybody, but so many of us for so many years have been told, you know, you do this, you go to school, you go to, you get your A-levels, you go to uni,
sentences.zh: 所以就业并不适合所有人，但我们中许多人多年来一直被告知，你知道，你这样做，你去上学，你去考 A-level，你去上大学，

sentences.en: you get a job, then you retire.
sentences.zh: 你找份工作，然后退休。

sentences.en: Like, those are your options, that's it.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的选择，仅此而已。

sentences.en: And I think it's really made us think, actually, I don't know, I don't know if I want that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的让我们开始思考，其实，我不知道，我不知道我是否想要那样。

sentences.en: And employment that's in a shared office where you have to manage the noise and the hubbub of everybody around you and the chance that they might pass you and make some inconsequential social chit-chat comments that doesn't suit how you function.
sentences.zh: 在共享办公室工作，你必须应对周围人的噪音和喧闹，还要应对他们经过时可能会跟你进行一些无关紧要的社交闲聊，这并不适合你的运作方式。

sentences.en: And then going, actually, I can do this work, I can be productive.
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，其实，我可以做这份工作，我可以很有成效。

sentences.en: And I don't, I'm not using up my social battery to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且我不需要消耗我的社交电池来完成它。

sentences.en: I can use my social batteries in ways that replenish me.
sentences.zh: 我可以以能让我恢复精力的方式使用我的社交电池。

sentences.en: When I was working in a shared office, people kind of, I don't know, like, people just like to talk, don't they?
sentences.zh: 当我在共享办公室工作时，人们，我不知道，人们就是喜欢聊天，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I like to talk as well.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢聊天。

sentences.en: But if I've got work to do as well, I almost had to get myself in work mode and wear my AirPods and risk being quite rude to people, because otherwise I would not get my work done.
sentences.zh: 但如果我还有工作要做，我几乎必须让自己进入工作模式，戴上 AirPods，冒着被认为很不礼貌的风险，否则我就无法完成工作。

sentences.en: And, you know, then, you know, the clients, my patients, don't get what they need.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，客户，我的病人，就得不到他们需要的服务。

sentences.en: They don't get their reports, they don't get their clinical notes done, and I'm in trouble.
sentences.zh: 他们拿不到报告，我的临床记录也写不完，我就有麻烦了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, like, and I'd have to explain to my colleagues, actually, when I've got my AirPods in, as much as I'd love to chat, I can't.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我必须向同事解释，其实，当我戴着 AirPods 时，尽管我很想聊天，但我不能。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's like, that's closing the door on your individual office, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，那就像是关上了你独立办公室的门，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, but if you haven't got one.
sentences.zh: 是的，但如果你没有独立办公室的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: So that's the sign of it, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是它的标志，绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So, yeah, like, if people are thinking, oh, yeah, that this could be worth exploring, is there a generic ballpark figure for what someone might be expecting to spend?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果人们在想，哦，是的，这值得探索，那么对于一个人可能预期的花费，有一个大概的数字吗？

sentences.en: It might be a range for an adult autism assessment.
sentences.zh: 对于成年人自闭症评估来说，可能是一个范围。

sentences.en: I think it is a range rather than a precise figure, but I would be expecting a roundabout, maybe a bit under, maybe a bit over £2,000 for it, which is a huge amount of resources.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个范围而不是一个精确的数字，但我预计大约在 2000 英镑左右，可能稍微少一点或多一点，这是一笔巨大的资源。

sentences.en: So if I was somebody in that, and you can definitely get it cheaper, I'm talking about services that are multidisciplinary and particularly strong,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我是当事人，虽然你肯定能找到更便宜的，但我说的是那些多学科且特别强大的服务，

sentences.en: you know, particularly thoughtfully and carefully, because that takes a lot of resources.
sentences.zh: 你知道，特别周到和谨慎的服务，因为那需要大量的资源。

sentences.en: I think if you're thinking about pursuing that speak to services that you find, ask them whether they fulfil what's called the NICE guidelines,
sentences.zh: 如果你正在考虑进行评估，请联系你找到的服务机构，询问他们是否符合所谓的 NICE 指南，

sentences.en: because those are the, as you'll know, the NICE guidelines, they describe what is required for any, for an assessment.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所知，NICE 指南描述了评估所需的条件。

sentences.en: And it means that if you're, if the service you go to fulfil those NICE guidelines, follow those NICE guidelines,
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你选择的服务机构符合这些 NICE 指南，遵循这些 NICE 指南，

sentences.en: the outcome has a better chance of being accepted in statutory services and in services you approach for things like accommodations and provisions on the basis of any diagnosis that's made.
sentences.zh: 那么评估结果在法定服务机构中，以及在你因任何诊断结果而寻求住宿和保障时，被接受的可能性就更大。

sentences.en: Yeah, so like anything, I guess, especially with the rise of kind of how popular talking about this is becoming in the media,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以像任何事情一样，我想，特别是在媒体上讨论这个话题变得如此流行的情况下，

sentences.en: we're likely to see very cheap, you know, assessment, diagnosis, processes, but, you know, cheap is not always best, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们很可能会看到非常便宜的评估和诊断流程，但便宜并不总是最好的，你知道。

sentences.en: Not always.
sentences.zh: 不总是。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's the price range that our assessments are in.
sentences.zh: 而且，这就是我们评估的价格范围。

sentences.en: So, of course, I'm going to tell you that those are the price range to imagine, but, and I think in, in, in services that develop to assess for autism,
sentences.zh: 所以，我当然会告诉你这是预期的价格范围，但我认为，在那些专门评估自闭症的服务机构中，

sentences.en: I think it's really important to think about what's required to make a sound and thorough and appropriate, valid assessment.
sentences.zh: 我认为思考什么才是做出稳健、彻底、适当且有效的评估所必需的，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: What are the extras that can really add depth and, and completion to, to someone's, to the outcome and someone's understanding of themselves,
sentences.zh: 有哪些额外的东西可以真正增加深度，并使评估结果和个人对自己的理解更加完整，

sentences.en: but aren't needed for diagnostic integrity.
sentences.zh: 但这些对于诊断的完整性来说并非必需。

sentences.en: And so each service and each practice will, will put a line in a slightly different place, put that line in a slightly different place, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为每个服务机构和每个诊所对这些额外内容的界定会略有不同。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I think there's so much skills and benefit in clinicians who have professional qualifications and have years of experience in that.
sentences.zh: 我认为那些拥有专业资质且具备多年相关经验的临床医生，能带来巨大的价值和益处。

sentences.en: So even when I was in the CAMHS team, there was, you know, a couple of consultant clinical psychologists,
sentences.zh: 所以即使是在我以前所在的儿童与青少年心理健康服务（CAMHS）团队里，也有几位临床心理学顾问，

sentences.en: a speech and language therapist who had worked in a qualified capacity for many, many years.
sentences.zh: 还有一位拥有多年专业执业经验的言语治疗师。

sentences.en: I think, yeah, two, two OTs actually, and then kind of CBT therapists and people that, you know, you've got all of those years of experience combined,
sentences.zh: 我想，还有两位职业治疗师，以及认知行为疗法（CBT）治疗师，他们加起来拥有非常丰富的经验，

sentences.en: but also experience of, of seeing people that are, you know, neurotypical as well, people across the lifespan,
sentences.zh: 而且他们也接触过神经典型人群，以及各个年龄段的人，

sentences.en: so that you're really getting a sense of, of whether this is something that's going to support and, and help that person.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的能感受到，这是否能真正支持和帮助到那个人。

sentences.en: And yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think when, when people don't have those levels of professional qualifications, they don't have that professional registration.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当人们没有达到这些专业资质水平，也没有获得专业注册时，

sentences.en: I think they just, they don't have the integrity and they, they don't have,
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们缺乏诚信，而且他们没有，

sentences.en: I don't think they've got the requisite skills personally to be doing the work that they are saying they are experts in always, you know?
sentences.zh: 我个人认为他们并不具备必要的技能，去从事那些他们自称是专家的工作，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And I think it's really difficult as well,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这确实非常困难，

sentences.en: because it leaves both, both the practitioners who are in that situation and the clients really vulnerable to having the outcomes challenged.
sentences.zh: 因为它让处于这种情况的从业者和客户都非常脆弱，容易受到质疑。

sentences.en: And, and that must be incredibly hard for people who have gone through a process to have the outcome challenged.
sentences.zh: 对于那些经历了整个流程却还要面对结果被质疑的人来说，这一定非常难受。

sentences.en: And I guess I would also say, Marianne, that the, the cost of it is a huge barrier.
sentences.zh: 我想我还要说的是，Marianne，成本是一个巨大的障碍。

sentences.en: And so there'll be many for whom that that's impossible.
sentences.zh: 所以对许多人来说，这根本是不可能的。

sentences.en: I think self-identifying as autistic, if you've done the work, if it fits your way of being,
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果你已经做了功课，如果这种自我认同符合你的生活方式，

sentences.en: if it just makes sense of the bits that didn't make sense beforehand, I think that it's valid.
sentences.zh: 如果它能让你之前想不通的事情变得合理，那么我认为这种自我认同是有效的。

sentences.en: It's okay to say that you consider yourself to be autistic.
sentences.zh: 你可以说你认为自己是自闭症人士，这没问题。

sentences.en: I wouldn't challenge that myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己不会去质疑这一点。

sentences.en: I think the value of having it clarified through an assessment process is that some autistic minds prefer certainty and so need an external person to go, yep, I agree.
sentences.zh: 我认为通过评估流程来明确诊断的价值在于，一些自闭症患者倾向于确定性，因此需要外部人员来确认：是的，我同意。

sentences.en: This is what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是如此。

sentences.en: You haven't fooled anyone.
sentences.zh: 你没有欺骗任何人。

sentences.en: You haven't exaggerated anything.
sentences.zh: 你没有夸大任何事情。

sentences.en: It is what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是这样。

sentences.en: So that can bring kind of internal peace to that identity kind of claim and also access to kind of the legal protections under the Equality Act,
sentences.zh: 所以这可以为这种身份认同带来内心的平静，也能让你获得《平等法案》下的法律保护，

sentences.en: because autism is legally classed as a, as a disability.
sentences.zh: 因为自闭症在法律上被归类为一种残疾。

sentences.en: I don't have, you don't have to agree that it inherently is, but it is legally classed as one.
sentences.zh: 你不必非要认同它本质上就是残疾，但它在法律上确实被这样归类。

sentences.en: So you do get protected by some legislation around kind of people providing support and accommodations to make sure that you thrive rather than burn out.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实会受到一些法律保护，比如要求他人提供支持和便利，确保你能茁壮成长而不是精疲力竭。

sentences.en: So I think there is real positives for having that formal process, but identifying it in yourself and noticing it in yourself and describing yourself that way is valid too.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为正式的评估流程确实有积极意义，但自我识别、自我察觉并以此描述自己也是有效的。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time and for helping us understand more about this.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间，并帮助我们更多地了解这一点。

sentences.en: Where's the best place for people to learn more about you and your work, Katie?
sentences.zh: Katie，人们去哪里能更多地了解你和你的工作呢？

sentences.en: So my website is theadolphuspractice.co.uk and we have a Facebook page, which is the Adolphus Practice and we're on Instagram as the.adolphuspractice.
sentences.zh: 我的网站是 theadolphuspractice.co.uk，我们有一个 Facebook 页面叫 The Adolphus Practice，我们的 Instagram 账号是 the.adolphuspractice。

sentences.en: So that's where you find us.
sentences.zh: 这就是找到我们的方式。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I will make sure that all of those details are on screen for YouTube and in the show notes and in description everywhere else.
sentences.zh: 我会确保所有这些详细信息都显示在 YouTube 屏幕上，并放在节目说明和描述栏里。

sentences.en: Thank you so much again for your time and for putting up with my voice, which almost abandoned us at times today as well.
sentences.zh: 再次非常感谢你抽出时间，还要忍受我今天几度快要失声的嗓音。

sentences.en: I think it's just about held on.
sentences.zh: 我想它总算是坚持下来了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Well, no worries.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time in listening or watching this episode.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你花时间收听或观看本期节目。

sentences.en: If you have found it helpful, please do drop me a like, a comment, a follow, a subscribe.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得有帮助，请务必给我点赞、评论、关注或订阅。

sentences.zh: 关注你欣赏的创作者的节目，真的是你能免费做的最暖心的事了。

sentences.en: And I would be so grateful if you could do that for me, please.
sentences.zh: 如果你能为我这样做，我会非常感激。

sentences.en: You might well be engaging with this episode because you are working in the mental health space.
sentences.zh: 你可能正在从事心理健康领域的工作，所以才关注这一期节目。

sentences.en: If you yourself have an autism diagnosis, you may wonder whether that would make you a good enough mental health professional.
sentences.zh: 如果你自己有自闭症诊断，你可能会怀疑这是否会让你成为一名优秀的心理健康专业人士。

sentences.en: And this is where I think the book, An Autistic Anthology, Neuro Narratives of Mental Health Professionals, is really worth checking out.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为《自闭症选集：心理健康专业人士的神经叙事》（An Autistic Anthology, Neuro Narratives of Mental Health Professionals）这本书非常值得一读的原因。

sentences.en: It is a collab, so to speak, between Nikita Shepardson, Dr. Vicky Jervis and myself.
sentences.zh: 这是 Nikita Shepardson、Vicky Jervis 博士和我共同合作的作品。

sentences.en: And it is real life look through the lens or for people who self-identify as being autistic and the way that they've seen the world,
sentences.zh: 它通过自闭症人士的视角，展现了他们的真实生活，以及他们看待世界的方式，

sentences.en: the way that it shaped their experiences and how they've gone on to successfully work in the mental health space.
sentences.zh: 这种方式如何塑造了他们的经历，以及他们如何成功地在心理健康领域工作。

sentences.en: We have psychologists in there.
sentences.zh: 书里有心理学家。

sentences.en: We have psychiatrists in there.
sentences.zh: 有精神科医生。

sentences.en: There's all sorts of people at different stages of their career.
sentences.zh: 还有各种处于职业生涯不同阶段的人。

sentences.en: And it is a fascinating read.
sentences.zh: 这是一本非常引人入胜的书。

sentences.en: So I hope you find that really useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你会觉得它很有用。

sentences.en: If you read it already, I would love if you'd put a review on Amazon and Goodreads.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经读过了，我很希望你能去亚马逊和 Goodreads 上写个书评。

sentences.en: If you would find future episodes on autism and being autistic or any element of kind of neurodiversity,
sentences.zh: 如果你想看到未来关于自闭症、自闭症身份或任何神经多样性相关话题的节目，

sentences.en: please do let me know by dropping me a comment on YouTube and or connecting with me on social media, where I am Dr. Marianne Trent everywhere.
sentences.zh: 请务必在 YouTube 上留言告诉我，或者在社交媒体上与我联系，我在所有平台上的名字都是 Dr. Marianne Trent。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being part of my world.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你成为我世界的一部分。

sentences.en: And I will look forward to bringing you the next episode of the Aspiring Psychologist podcast, which will be available from 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我很期待为你带来下一期《有抱负的心理学家》播客，它将于周六上午 10 点在 YouTube 上线，

sentences.en: on Saturdays on YouTube and wherever you get your podcasts from 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 并于周一上午 6 点在各大播客平台发布。

sentences.en: on Monday.
sentences.zh: 保重。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 善待自己。

sentences.en: Be kind to yourself.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能通过出卖时间之外的方式赚钱，会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家 Marianne Trent 博士，我从 2019 年开始开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个激动人心的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One to Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: Sophie Foote 的“一对多”（One to Many）项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
